region.text: Tidore island, the Gamrange area of south-east Halmahera and the islands close by

ledger.note: 1081: the first king, Sahjati (Muhammad Naqil), by local tradition. The first king 'is dated 1081 in local tradition' (the page calls the accuracy 'debatable'); infobox 'Established 1081?/1450'.
1578: Tidore lets the Portuguese build a fort on its island. 'The Tidorese allowed the Portuguese to build a fort on their island in 1578.' Hatched as a foreign post.
1605: the Dutch expel the Portuguese from Tidore. The Dutch 'conquered Ambon and Tidore in 1605, expelling the Portuguese'.

c. 1606: the Spanish, allied with Tidore, are on its island. The Ternate page has Spain capturing the Ternate fort in 1606 'while Spain was allied with Tidore', and 'The Spanish abandoned Ternate and Tidore in 1663'; the Maluku page has Iberian rule restored 'in parts of North Maluku up to 1663'. No page dates the arrival on Tidore: the year is the Ternate capture, a bridging reading.
1666: the last Spanish leave. 'The Spanish decided to withdraw in 1662, carried out in 1663-1666'; the Ternate page has them gone in 1663.

1700: East Seram is granted to Tidore. East Seram 'had been granted Tidore in 1700' (neither the Tidore nor the Nuku page names the grantor: the VOC as counterpart is the researcher's reading; confidence lowered to 2 by the se-02-x review); 'At times, Tidore controlled East Seram'.
1768: Tidore cedes Seram to the Dutch. 'In 1768, the Dutch forced Sultan Jamaluddin to cede his rights to Seram, which enraged Nuku'; the Tidore page has East Seram ceded under a treaty of 1768.

region.text: Patani in Halmahera, Raja Ampat and Seram, from which Nuku led the rebellion

ledger.note: 1780: Nuku leaves Tidore and raises a rebellion. He 'left Tidore Island in 1780, sailing with his followers to' Patani in Halmahera, rejecting the new treaty of 1780 that reduced 'Tidore from a Dutch ally to a vassal state'; he was proclaimed 'King of the Papuans' and led the rebellion 'from the Raja Ampat and Seram Islands'.
1797: Nuku occupies Bacan. 'Bacan was occupied with the assistance of English country traders'; he also occupied Jailolo in Halmahera 'with British support' (undated on the page, not drawn).

region.text: Patani in Halmahera, Raja Ampat and Seram, from which Nuku led the rebellion

ledger.note: April 1797: Nuku's fleet reaches Tidore. 'In April the rebel fleet finally reached Tidore, whose Sultan Kamaluddin had already fled to safety in Ternate'; Nuku is enthroned (reign table 1797-1805), so the rebel zone merges into the sultanate.

June 1801: Tidore and the British take Ternate. The 'Dutch defenders finally surrendered in June 1801' to Nuku's forces (Tidore page: 'Ternate was captured by the British and Tidorese after a long siege').
1802: the Peace of Amiens lets the Dutch retake their Maluku posts, ending the capture of Ternate.

1806: the Dutch drive out Sultan Zainal Abidin. 'A new Dutch attack drove out his brother and successor Sultan Zainal Abidin from Tidore in 1806'; the Tidore page: 'Tidore was lost in 1806', and the sultan died in exile in 1810.
1806: Bacan leaves Nuku's hands with the Dutch return; the page gives no date for the end of the Bacan occupation (bridging).
1811: a sultan sits again on Tidore. The reign table has Muhammad Tahir from 1811; the page gives no date for the end of the Dutch occupation of the island.

wars.name: Dutch conquest of Ambon and Tidore
wars.outcome: The Dutch 'conquered Ambon and Tidore in 1605, expelling the Portuguese' from the fort Tidore had allowed in 1578.
wars.note: The Maluku page puts Ambon and Tidore together; the Tidore page puts Ambon under the VOC in 1605 without Tidore authority there.

wars.name: Nuku's rebellion

zones.text: Patani in Halmahera, Raja Ampat and Seram, from which Nuku led the rebellion

wars.outcome: Nuku, allied with the British, took Tidore (April 1797), Bacan (1797) and Ternate (June 1801); he died on 14 November 1805 and the Dutch drove his brother out in 1806.
wars.note: The Tidore page dates the rebellion from 1780; Nuku's page has the 1780 treaty that reduced Tidore to a vassal.

wars.name: Spanish alliance and withdrawal (Tidore)
wars.outcome: Tidore's 'loose alliance' with Spain against Ternate and the Dutch ended with the Spanish withdrawal decided in 1662 and carried out in 1663-1666.
wars.note: No Spanish fort on Tidore is dated on the page.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; island discs and provinces. The treaties of 1667 and 1780 are not boundaries.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for Tidore. Wikidata id not looked up (wikidata.org unreachable): null. Start 1081 is the page's local-tradition date for the first king (debatable); the infobox also gives 1450 and the page puts Islam in the late 15th century. End 1905: the infobox runs to 1967. The pages give no frontier for any date; the shapes are discs on Tidore with the Gamrange coast of Halmahera. The Papuan claim (by 1849) is an upper bound and a tint at confidence 1. Sultanate of Bacan (occupation 1797-1806) and Nuku's rebel Tidore (1780-1797) may need dossiers (sultanate-of-bacan; nuku-rebellion, type rebel). The Tidore page has Jailolo occupied by Nuku, the 1657 clove-eradication agreement and the 1667 contract: no territory. Overlap with the sultanate-of-ternate shape on the facing Halmahera shore is unavoidable at this resolution. Gazetteer: Labuha (Bacan), Patani (Halmahera), Seram, Raja Ampat, Halmahera, Gamrange are not in places/regions.
